## Active roadmap — full framework audit, 2026-10-04

This is the **only master** for reusable simulation/colony/RTS framework work. P1–P6 retain their IDs;
P7–P12 extend the roadmap. All reusable engine logic belongs in Beep.SimEngine. A game contributes
engine-side domain providers and explicitly listed JSON, not gameplay inside a host/demo/harness.
SimEngine is simulation-first. The business/Tycoon module is optional: survival/resource-only games
need no money, prices, buyers, sellers or economy service. Values, accounts, production income,
construction/manufacturing/running monetary costs and trading are independent opt-ins. Selecting the
module does not enable them all. Explicit Tycoon activation enables its actual advanced providers
through that same module/contracts/accounts, not a second economy.
Physical resources, supply, movement, jobs and timing remain authoritative engine mechanisms.
Population/combat/spatial maps are optional capabilities. Unmonetized games omit business entirely;
they do not need a fake zero-price catalog, FreeEconomy instance or market to construct from resources.

Planning deliverables are complete: [source audit](ENGINE_AUDIT.md), staged designs and
[offline help with graphs and quick setup](../../help/index.html). This is **not implementation completion**.

Execution is not numeric: **P2 → P3 → P4 composition → P7 → P4 DAG → P8 → P9 → P10 →
P11/P12 → P5 → P6**. P4 composition has no resource dependency; P4 graph acquisition uses P7.
This split avoids a circular phase dependency. Stage gates run throughout; P6 release closure comes last.

### Ownership decisions locked by this revision

ResolvedContent remains the resource catalog. IInventory providers own stock. Existing reservation
state gains owned tokens; a coordinator cannot mirror balances. WorkBoard/WorkSystem own graph/job
execution. ProductionSystem is replaced by one TransformerManager, not supplemented. Entity.Update
alone commits entity state. ContentSet/ContentTypes remain the master JSON pipeline. New optional
mechanisms live in this framework runtime; domain science/playbooks live in engine extensions.

No compatibility aliases/loaders, duplicate schedulers, implicit defaults, instant gameplay fallback,
platform adapters or platform map-size caps. Actual checked numeric/allocation/protocol budgets remain
explicit. Tycoon and the older sibling engine are untouched. Documentation/examples do not implement
the proposed future API.

## Historical extraction ledger

The following narrative preserves earlier slice evidence. The active table and baseline above take
precedence; historical counts do not establish current-source correctness or close planned stages.

## Direction

Extract the active v2 engine from OilFieldDays into `Beep.SimEngine`. Make OilFieldDays an
oil-and-gas extension using the same public contracts available to another simulation game.
Keep one implementation owner per responsibility. Do not copy the engine, retain an old facade,
or create a compatibility layer.

This is the single tracker for this extraction. Stage documents own detailed acceptance criteria;
the original v2 revision tracker links here and does not duplicate this backlog.

## Completion rules

- A stage is complete only after its implementation and named acceptance gates pass.
- Record source revision or working-tree identity, exact commands, failures, exclusions, and duration.
- Preserve existing test coverage; a changed test count alone is not evidence of lost or improved coverage.
- No historical pass count closes an unimplemented stage. Report focused and full verification separately.
- An oil-only policy must never become a mandatory framework rule.
- Framework rules and oil rules run inside their engine assemblies. A client drives input/time and presents
  immutable results; it does not decide work eligibility, costs, state, travel, hazards, or outcomes.

## Start conditions and decisions

1. Before moving files, capture the dirty source inventory and inspect target collisions again.
2. Use the requested target path. Do not initialize Git or configure a remote without an explicit request.
   Extraction can be verified locally before deciding repository publication.
3. Initially use a direct project reference from OilFieldDays to the standalone framework. Package
   publication/version distribution is a later decision, not a second simultaneous implementation path.
4. Read existing activity-DAG/content plans and merge their responsibilities into P4. Do not implement
   a parallel workflow executor or preserve superseded design documents as competing authorities.
5. The older sibling engine, Tycoon, renderers, Unity, and Godot remain outside this extraction.

## Final acceptance

Current implemented slices: P1 inventories 121 original files, moves the runtime/generic suites once,
renames consumers, and centralizes test helpers/build policies. P2 removes oil friendship and exposes
seat-validated `World.ViewFor`. Counter and colony modules compile in an independent non-friend
assembly; boundary/privacy and physical work checks pass.

Capability slice: worker/role, mobility, inventory, inlet/outlet, transporter and network-port contracts
use existing entity slots/indexes and state. Explicit JSON-authored transport uses the existing cargo
inventory. Independent workers/endpoints execute standard timed work, physical haul/stock commands,
entity-owned state projection and save/load continuation without scheduler edits or built-in components.
Every outlet is an inlet; duplicate capability owners fail content resolution before play.

Composition slice: canonical dependency order and exact code/content module versions; schema-1 master
manifest includes code-only modules; active content providers/generators and document ownership;
frozen declarations and single-owner service/command registrations; missing providers and persistent
codec collisions fail before Initialize. Saves/hashes/lockstep record module versions. Standard work
requires an explicit economy policy. Oil gameplay now queries the available inventory/worker contracts.

Inventory completion: producer validation and demolition use IInventory, prototype compatibility uses
IInletPortDefinition, and production validates whole output compatibility plus promised capacity before
committing items/vehicles. Read-only production views expose authoritative private operating facts.
An independently compiled inventory produces, blocks, resumes and survives physical demolition/recovery
through the unchanged production/work/logistics owners and the existing save/hash path.

Module registrations now capture immutable identity and dependencies before declaration. Canonical
selection, manifest checks, saves and peers use the same registrations, even if external modules later
change their getters or supplied lists. Invalid graphs run no declaration callbacks.

Mobility/supply completion: MovementSystem dispatches IMobility.Advance in its existing phase; built-in
Mover owns its route algorithm, and independent providers own their movement state. Rollout reads
IMobilityDefinition, never an implicit land fallback. ISupplier performs paid physical pickup against the
declared economy; Job.Purchase distinguishes it from owned stock, survives saves and participates in hashes.
External lane vehicles and finite suppliers prove timed production/travel, route refusal/change, payment
refusal, protected stock, owned free transfers and deterministic saved continuation without scheduler edits.

Typed roles: WorkerRoleId is a public immutable identity, not a closed enum or table position.
WorkerRoleDef is authored under worker_roles, including a manifest-owned oil/worker-roles.json catalog.
Workers, jobs, steps, generated line/demolition plans and views use the same typed references. Unknown
and duplicate memberships/referrals refuse content or runtime posting; timed stages use explicit None.
An independently compiled worker performs a newly authored module.fabricate requirement with physical
travel/construction and identical saved continuation, without scheduler edits. No old string-role API remains.

Requirement seam: module-owned WorkRequirementDef subclasses resolve through existing content indexes;
StepDef references and generated plans validate the same authority. The sole board evaluator drives
typed private previews and pre-consumption/continuous execution guards. Paused jobs retain workers,
progress and existing save/hash state; cancellation releases them. Machines travel and wait physically.
Independent providers prove authored guards, measured shortages, invalid references, pure diagnostics,
timed work, travel, generated plans and deterministic saved continuation. This is not a second DAG executor.

Operation/signal seam: named capability IDs select a single provider within the existing entity parts.
An offshore platform exposes both power and production without ambiguous implicit selection. Producer
controls are JSON-authored, bounded, command-owned and saved; disabling retains work without spending or
progressing. Typed signal definitions share the content registry; unavailable bindings are explicit,
never fabricated zero readings. Private immutable views and previews use the same control validation.
An external non-friend operation owns its own engine update and codec, without a producer wrapper.
FieldPlayer now reads actual engine power-operation facts instead of guessing from fuel inventory.

Authored effects/response seam: JSON providers resolve through the existing content indexes; delegate
registration is removed. Composition validation refuses missing effects before Initialize. Incident
providers own state/codecs and post physical normal orders with saved source/episode bindings; stale
or unfinished work cannot clear incidents. Oil wear/storyteller consumers use those contracts.

Owned views: existing registry entries capture stable ID, schema version, contract and module owner.
Required features validate before Initialize; declarations freeze. PlayerView exposes immutable sorted
metadata and scoped lazy features, never factories. Standard, proof and oil registrations migrated in place.

Owned events: the existing bus entries declare payload identity/schema/provider; subscriptions record
stable handler identity/module owner during composition. Missing/inactive providers and collisions
refuse before Initialize. Declarations freeze; dispatch remains global publication order with nested
events on the same pass. Exception cleanup clears every published queue, including undelivered types.
Private delegates are not exposed by immutable player diagnostics. No implicit/anonymous path remains.

Owned state codecs: existing component declarations, system slots and persistent service bindings
capture stable identity/schema/module metadata. Explicit versions are mandatory; aliases share one
captured codec, generated parts require active declarations. World.Sync validates the canonical saved
manifest and system scheduling before restoring any payload. Immutable view metadata exposes no
providers. Save/load/hash still use the same Sync per owner; no legacy reader or parallel state store.

Historical next-action note: subsequent P2 binding work is recorded in the active section above;
the current next mechanism is P3 authored time/durations. Conditional automation is detailed in P10.
Configurable time, nonspatial worlds, the new activity DAG, generic
mechanism promotions, expanded mod proof and replay/end-to-end gates are not yet implemented.

A clean standalone build and test run needs no OilFieldDays source or content. OilFieldDays builds
against the standalone engine and retains its physical, timed gameplay. At least two independently
composed non-oil fixtures exercise the framework, including one without a tile map. A separate module
assembly extends workers, workflows, endpoints, state, signals, and responses without engine edits or
friend access. Save/load, replay, lockstep, isolation, and ownership gates pass with no duplicated engine.
